A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
curiosity is an intrinsic reward signal for learning progress, which is used to drive learning in the absence of task relevant rewards.
curiosity is a fundamental mechanism to bootstrap learning in complex environments, by fostering exploration of the diversity of behavioural skills and by ignoring deceptive local rewards.
Curiosity is a fundamental mechanism that enables organisms to discover and learn new skills, and to solve complex problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mechanisms of curiosity are not just about the discovery of rewards, but also about the discovery of skills and knowledge, and that curiosity is a fundamental driver of self organization and development in organisms.
curiosity is not a single thing, but a set of mechanisms, which can be studied in isolation or in combination.
curiosity is a fundamental mechanism to learn about the world and about ourselves in order to make discoveries.
